### B. Reproducing kernel Hilbert space

Next, we introduce the necessary RKHS notation. We denote a symmetric and strictly positive definite kernel function by \( k : \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}\) and define the canonical features \(\phi_x\) for \( x \in \mathbb{R}^n\) by \(\phi_x = k(x, \cdot)\). Further, for the data \(\mathcal{X}\) and the kernel k we define the kernel matrix

\[
K_{\mathcal{X}} = 
\begin{bmatrix}
k(x_1, x_1) & \dots & k(x_d, x_1) \\
\vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
k(x_1, x_d) & \dots & k(x_d, x_d)
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

Importantly, the kernel k induces a Hilbert space of functions (\(\mathcal{H}, \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\mathcal{H}\) with reproducing property \(f(x) = \langle f, \phi_x \rangle_\mathcal{H}\) for all \( x \in \mathbb{R}^n\) and \(f \in \mathcal{H}\) [22]. Throughout the paper, we consider the RKHS \(\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{N}_s\) induced by piecewise-polynomial and compactly supported kernel functions based on the Wendland radial basis functions \(\Theta_{n,s} : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}\) with state dimension \(n \in \mathbb{N}\) and smoothness degree \(s \in \mathbb{N}\). More precisely, \(\Theta_{n,s}(x) = \theta_{n,s}(\|x\|)\), where we refer to [22, Corollary 9.14] for the definition of \(\theta_{n,s}\) for general \(n\) and \(s \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}\). Importantly, \(\theta_{n,s} \in C^{2s}([0, \infty), \mathbb{R})\), i.e., it possesses \(2s\) continuous derivatives [22, Lemma 9.8]. As an example, for \(n \le 3\) and \(s = 1\), \(\theta_{n,1} \in C^2([0, \infty), \mathbb{R})\) is twice continuously differentiable and defined by

\[
\theta_{n,1}(r) =
\begin{cases}
(1-r)^4(4r+1) & \text{for } r < 1, \\
0 & \text{for } r \ge 1.
\end{cases}
\]

Then, the induced Wendland kernel is given by \(k(x, y) = \theta_{n,s}(\|x - y\|)\) for \( x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n\).

**Assumption 3.** The smoothness degree \(s \in \mathbb{N}\) of the Wendland kernels satisfies \(s \ge 1\).

This assumption ensures a sufficiently smooth kernel function, i.e., it is at least twice continuously differentiable.

**Lemma 4.** Let Assumption 3 hold. Then, the canonical features \(\phi_{x_j}, j \in [1:d]\), admit a local norm bound on their Hessian matrix on \(\mathbb{X}\), i.e.,

\[\| 
\begin{array}{ccccc}
    \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) & \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_1 & \dots & \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_1 \partial x_n \\
    \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \\
    \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_n \partial x_1 & \dots & \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_n^2 &
\end{array}
\end{array}
\begin{equation}
=
\begin{cases}
    \| \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_n^2 & \dots & \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_n \partial x_1 \\
    \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
    \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_n^2 \partial x_1 & \dots & \partial^2 \phi_{x_j}(x) / \partial x_n^2 &
\end{cases}
\begin{equation}
\le D_\phi (6)
\end{equation}\]

for all \(j \in [1:d]\) and \(x \in \mathbb{X}\) with some \(D_\phi > 0\).

**Proof**. Observe \(\phi_{x_j}(x) = k(x_j, x) = \theta_{n,k}(\|x_j - x\|) \in C^{2s}([0, \infty), \mathbb{R})\) and \(s \ge 1\) due to Assumption 3, i.e., the canonical features are at least twice continuously differentiable. Since the region \(\mathbb{X}\) is compact, we directly conclude the norm bound (6) for some \(D_\phi > 0\). □

The native RKHS norm \(\| \cdot \|_{\mathcal{N}_s}\) is induced by the abstract inner product and thus typically hard to compute. For Wendland kernels, this norm is equivalent to a fractional Sobolev norm using an extension operator [22, Corollary 10.48].

Each SS handles the packet processing similar to the stroage processing network. When processing a packet, the PS first verifies that the packet's label matches the "Local Name" assigned to the stream, then selects the applicable instance. If there is a disabled stream, the PS initializes the variable stream_num for each SS instance to -1, sets the packet receiver address for this stream to the one assigned to instance, and records the sender address. ## 6 Evaluation
In this section, we give a detailed assessment of the layout, fault tolerance, and resource utilization of the SLMS and compare it with what has been reported in the literature. We use an accumulator model as the basis for evaluation, and we also give an analysis of the PS traffic load and delay. For evaluation, the SLMS uses a TDMA virtual machine (VM), and the protocol suite consists of the Kernel Extensible firmware (KEX) discussed in Section 4.

### Layout of Processor #0
The LSMS consists of * * A 32Mhz embedded TURBO-Peripheral Processor (TDP) that serves as the LCMS' main CPU. * * A 24Mhz TDU to perform kernel operations and analyze Channel State Information (CSI). * * A 13Mhz Phytomet head (PHY), whose purpose is to monitor PHY transmissions for user acknowledgement (ACK). Astrophon also comprises a TEN device and a Casing Alarms (CARS) box. These are separate boxes that are powered on/off. Furthermore, the rack-mount PSx (M210), STX (M250), and OPSx (M359) are equipped with two circuits and four LZBs.
